headline: Telangana HC: Section 143(2) notice by notified Prescribed Authority valid in centralised case
reference: M/s. Fusion Health Care Pvt. Ltd. vs Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle-2(2), Telangana High Court, W.P. No. 31603 of 2026, order dated 13.10.2026
summary_points: Issue: Is a s.143(2) notice for AY 2025-26 issued by the Prescribed Income-tax Authority void because the case was centralised with the Assessing Officer?
Held: The notice was not without jurisdiction; an officer notified by CBDT under Rule 12E can issue it, and 'as the case may be' does not give the AO exclusive competence.
The Court agreed with the Delhi HC in Ambience (P) Ltd., which rejected the argument that only the AO or NaFAC officers can issue such notices.
The writ was held premature: s.142(1) notices only seek information and are not assessment orders, so the petition was dismissed.
Practical impact: jurisdictional objections must be raised before the AO and in appeals before CIT(A) and ITAT after assessment, not by early writ petitions.
who_is_affected: Assessees, especially those in centralised search cases, who receive s.143(2) or s.142(1) notices from an officer other than their jurisdictional Assessing Officer.
action_required: Respond to such notices on time, check the CBDT notification authorising the issuing officer, and keep jurisdictional objections for the assessment and appellate stages.

social.linkedin:
Telangana High Court has dismissed a writ by Fusion Health Care Pvt Ltd challenging a Section 143(2) notice for AY 2025-26.

The petitioner's case was centralised with a Central Circle Assessing Officer after a search. The s.143(2) notice, however, came from an officer notified by CBDT as the Prescribed Income-tax Authority under Rule 12E. The petitioner argued that only the AO could issue it, and that the limitation under the proviso had expired.

The Bench held that the notice was not without jurisdiction. The expression 'as the case may be' in s.143(2) does not make the AO the exclusive authority in centralised cases. The Court agreed with the Delhi High Court's reasoning in Ambience (P) Ltd.

The Court also found the writ premature. The s.142(1) notices only call for information, and every objection can be raised before the AO and then in appeal before CIT(A) and ITAT.

Takeaway: do not rely on an early writ to attack the issuing officer of a s.143(2) notice. Check the CBDT notification and respond on time.

Please verify with the official source and the full order before acting.
